statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD are both inside the CME weekend halt: cash equities closed at 20:00Z on Friday and the E-mini settled at 21:00Z, and no venue quotes either instrument at any point in this 24-hour window.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold in every published slot because a no-retracement price path cannot form while quoting is suspended. The macro stack carried into the break - a unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% with 16 of 18 participants projecting a further increase, a 10-year that settled 4.998% after tagging 5.008%, WTI at 100.30 dollars on a third consecutive decline, Bab el-Mandeb under Houthi control and a Washington summit scheduled for 24 September - is expressed through Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. Gap risk expresses at the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, 21 hours beyond the final slot published here.
headline: A settled contract, a 4.998% 10-year and a 14.81 VIX sit out the weekend halt with Tail pinned at its floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67%, finishing near the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range against a 29,447.00 previous close. The E-mini NQ contract settled at 29,955.00, up 0.71%, having ranged 29,648.00-29,993.25. VIX eased 4.08% to 14.81 and closed at its session low, a subdued mark against the current macro backdrop. The broader tape was mixed rather than directional: the S&P 500 rose 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.39% to 26,522.55, while the Dow slipped 0.18% to 51,682.64. Friday also cleared about 6.2 trillion dollars of options notional in the September triple witching, a positioning reset that is a conditional sensitivity for the new week rather than an observed condition now. Internals were rotational: semiconductor equipment rose 4.85% and semiconductors 1.87% while both software groups fell about 1%, and megacaps finished split four to four with AVGO up 2.97% and MU up 3.92% against META down 2.43% and QCOM down 5.82%. Rates remain the dominant carried driver. The FOMC raised its target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous vote, its first increase in three years, with 16 of 18 participants projecting another hike this year; the 10-year settled 4.998% after tagging 5.008% intraday and the 2-year ended near 4.739%, with the H.15 release through 17 September showing 4.94% and 4.67% and a 3.88% effective funds rate. WTI settled 100.30 dollars, down 1.58% and a third consecutive decline, with Brent at 103.87, as work to restore Saudi East-West pipeline capacity eased supply fears; Bab el-Mandeb has been under Houthi control since mid-September and no new escalation has been verified since Friday's settlement. None of this can transmit to either instrument inside the halt. The published window runs from 02:00Z Saturday to 01:00Z Sunday, and futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, 21 hours after the final slot. Tail is therefore held between 5 and 7 across all slots, Stress decays from 24 into the low band and returns to 25, Confidence declines from 82 to 75 purely as a function of evidence age, dominant mode is normal throughout and no danger window is published.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held a 5-19 band and Stress ran between 25 and 51, peaking near 51 through the European morning and the U.S. afternoon before falling away to 33, 28, 27, 26 and 25 in the final five hours as cash trading ended and the contract settled. Confidence sat between 83 and 88 throughout. Dominant mode rotated from normal across the Asian and early European hours to trend-up into the U.S. pre-open, to mixed through the cash session as leadership narrowed, briefly back to trend-up into the close, then to normal once the expiry cleared and venues shut.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour window falls inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z, the E-mini settled at 21:00Z, and futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, 21 hours after the final slot published here. Tail is held between 5 and 7 across all slots, with a marginal lift from midday Saturday that reflects the growing stock of unpriced weekend information rather than any observed structure. Stress decays from 24, troughs at 20 across the middle of Saturday, and edges back to 25 as the new week's agenda approaches. Confidence stays in the high band and drifts from 82 to 75 purely as a function of evidence age. Dominant mode is normal in every slot and no danger window is published, because a pathological price path cannot form while no venue quotes.
